title_en: Guangxi Beisheng Group Co., Ltd. v. Beihai Weihao Real Estate Development Company and Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Livestock Products Import and Export Beihai Company — dispute over land use right transfer contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 36 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC provides: '...The capacity for civil rights and capacity for civil conduct of a legal person shall commence upon its establishment and shall cease upon its termination.' Article 38 of the Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration of the PRC provides: 'Upon approval of the cancellation of registration by the company registration authority, the company shall be terminated.' Therefore, a legal person that has been revoked of its business license according to law but has not undergone liquidation or completed cancellation of registration is not considered to have been terminated and still enjoys the capacity for civil rights and capacity for civil conduct in civil litigation according to law. When such a legal person enters into a contract dispute with others, it shall participate in civil litigation in its own name. Since its establishing unit is not a party to the contract, it does not have the qualification as a litigation subject.

full_text_en:
Guangxi Beisheng Group Co., Ltd. v. Beihai Weihao Real Estate Development Company and Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Animal By-Products Import and Export Beihai Company — dispute over land use right transfer contract

Ruling Summary

I. Article 36 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC provides: "... the capacity for civil rights and capacity for civil conduct of a legal person shall arise upon its establishment and shall cease upon its termination." Article 38 of the Regulations of the PRC on the Administration of Company Registration provides: "A company shall terminate upon the approval of its deregistration by the company registration authority." Therefore, where a legal person has been lawfully revoked of its business license but has not undergone liquidation nor completed deregistration procedures, it is not terminated and still enjoys the capacity for civil rights and capacity for civil conduct in litigation. Where such a legal person is involved in a contract dispute with another party, it shall participate in civil litigation in its own name. Its founding entity, not being a party to the contract, does not have the qualification to be a party to the litigation.

II. Only the people's court and arbitration institutions have the authority to determine whether a contract is valid; the parties to a contract do not have the right to confirm the validity of the contract. A void contract is void ab initio. Where a party requests confirmation that a contract is void, such request shall not be subject to the statutory limitation period. However, after the contract is confirmed void, where a party requests the return of property and compensation for losses, the provisions of the law on the statute of limitations shall apply.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 104

Appellant (defendant at first instance): Guangxi Beisheng Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 168 Beihai Avenue, Beihai City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
Legal representative: He Yuliang, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Bo, lawyer of Beijing Tianru Law Firm.

Appellee (plaintiff at first instance): Beihai Weihao Real Estate Development Company, domiciled at 9th Floor, Port Building, Sichuan Road, Beihai City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
Legal representative: Diao Jiangnan, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Li Chongwen, lawyer of Beijing Kevin Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Hu Xiaoshun, lawyer of Beijing Kevin Law Firm.

Appellee (plaintiff at first instance): Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Animal By-Products Import and Export Beihai Company, domiciled at 9th Floor, Port Building, Sichuan Road, Beihai City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
Legal representative: Peng Jialong, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Li Chongwen, lawyer of Beijing Kevin Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Hu Xiaoshun, lawyer of Beijing Kevin Law Firm.

In the case concerning a dispute over a land use right transfer contract between appellant Guangxi Beisheng Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Beisheng Group) and appellees Beihai Weihao Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Weihao Company) and Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Animal By-Products Import and Export Beihai Company (hereinafter referred to as Beihai Company), the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region rendered the Civil Judgment (2005) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 3 on September 20, 2005. Beisheng Group, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegiate panel and held a hearing on February 10, 2006. The agent ad litem of Beisheng Group, Zhang Bo, and the agents ad litem of Weihao Company and Beihai Company, Li Chongwen and Hu Xiaoshun, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial: On March 3, 1993, Beisheng Group and Weihao Company entered into the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement," stipulating that the two parties would cooperatively develop 150 mu of land within the township enterprise city area; Weihao Company would pay cooperative development fees at the standard of RMB 205,000 per mu, totaling RMB 30.75 million; within two working days after the agreement was signed, Weihao Company would pay Beisheng Group a deposit of RMB 5 million as earnest money, and at the same time deliver the original blueprint of the land and the land cooperative development agreement signed between Beisheng Group and the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Beihai City Township Enterprise City Investment Promotion Center (hereinafter referred to as the Investment Promotion Center) to Weihao Company for safekeeping; Beisheng Group, in principle, after receiving the deposit, would handle from the Investment Promotion Center the blueprint and contract conversion in the name of Weihao Company as the holder of the 150 mu of land, with the handling fees borne by Beisheng Group; Weihao Company would pay another RMB 10 million within 10 days after signing the agreement, and the remaining RMB 15.75 million would be paid in full before May 1, 1993; Beisheng Group would handle the blueprint and contract conversion, with a deadline of no more than 13 days (from the date of signing the agreement); if overdue, Beisheng Group would compensate Weihao Company RMB 1 million, but this contract would remain valid and enforceable; after Weihao Company paid the full amount, Beisheng Group, at Weihao Company's request, agreed to transfer the land use right to Weihao Company; Weihao Company would provide all documents including project approval necessary for handling the red-line map and land use certificate, and Beisheng Group would be responsible for handling the red-line map and land use certificate for Weihao Company; the agreement would take effect upon signature, sealing, and payment of the deposit. On the same day, the parties also signed a "Supplementary Agreement" stipulating that Beisheng Group and the Investment Promotion Center were cooperating in the development of the 150 mu of land, and Beisheng Group still owed 50% of the cooperative development fee, i.e., RMB 6 million. Before Weihao Company paid the full amount by May 1, 1993, any losses from Beisheng Group's overdue payment of the land cooperative development fee would be borne by Beisheng Group itself; if the Investment Promotion Center increased the land price, the increased portion would be borne by Beisheng Group; if the land was taken back, Beisheng Group should refund all amounts received to Weihao Company at the time the loss occurred, and compensate RMB 5 million within 5 days; if Weihao Company failed to pay Beisheng Group in full before May 1, 1993, Weihao Company would compensate RMB 5 million. On the same day, Beisheng Group delivered the original land schematic diagram to Weihao Company. Diao Jiangnan, the legal representative of Weihao Company, issued a receipt.

After the contract was signed, Weihao Company paid RMB 5 million, RMB 10 million, and RMB 10 million to Beisheng Group on March 4, March 13, and April 30, 1993, respectively, and Beisheng Group issued receipts for the payments. However, Beisheng Group did not handle the blueprint and contract conversion as agreed, nor did it handle the land use certificate for Weihao Company. Beisheng Group has not obtained the land use right for the disputed land to date, nor has it developed or utilized the disputed land. Both parties confirmed in court that Weihao Company had never asserted its rights against Beisheng Group before the litigation.

The court of first instance also found: Weihao Company was established and sponsored by Beihai Company, with the nature of a wholly people-owned enterprise legal person, and its supervisory authority was Beihai Company. Because Weihao Company failed to submit annual industrial and commercial inspections as required, on November 26, 2003, the Beihai City Administration for Industry and Commerce, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, issued an administrative penalty decision revoking Weihao Company's business license, but no liquidation group has been established for liquidation to date. Before January 1, 1997, the name of Beisheng Group was Zhejiang Guangsha Construction Group Beihai Company; on January 1, 1997, it changed to Guangxi Beihai Zhejiang Guangsha Construction Co., Ltd.; on August 23, 2002, it changed to Guangxi Beisheng Enterprise (Group) Co., Ltd.; on September 19, 2002, it changed again to Beisheng Group.

The court of first instance further found: On January 26, 2000, the Intermediate People's Court of Beihai City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, in the case of Liuzhou Hengtong Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Hengtong Company) v. Weihao Company and Chengdu Sanye Investment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanye Company) concerning a dispute over a land use right transfer contract, rendered the Civil Judgment (1999) Bei Min Chu Zi No. 66, determining that the 150 mu of land transferred by Weihao Company to Hengtong Company was acquired under the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed with Beisheng Group on March 3, 1993. However, Weihao Company and Sanye Company, without having obtained the land use right for that land, signed a land use right transfer agreement with Hengtong Company, and did not complete the land use right procedures during the first instance; therefore, the land use right transfer contract was void. The judgment ordered Weihao Company to return the land payment of RMB 28.2 million and interest thereon received from Hengtong Company. This judgment has become effective.

Weihao Company and Beihai Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance alleging: On March 3, 1993, Weihao Company signed the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" with the predecessor of Beisheng Group, Zhejiang Guangsha Construction Group Beihai Company, stipulating that the two parties would cooperatively develop 150 mu of land within the Beihai Township Enterprise City area; Weihao Company would pay development fees to Beisheng Group at the standard of RMB 205,000 per mu, and Beisheng Group would handle the land use right in the name of Weihao Company. After the agreement was signed, Weihao Company paid a total of RMB 25 million, but Beisheng Group failed to perform its contractual obligations. Subsequently, Weihao Company discovered that Beisheng Group had no right to sign the cooperative development agreement, and the agreement violated mandatory legal provisions and was a void contract. Since Weihao Company had not participated in annual industrial and commercial inspections for two years, its founding unit, Beihai Company, together with Weihao Company, is now liquidating Weihao Company's claims and debts. Therefore, they requested: 1. Confirmation that the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed by the parties is void; 2. An order that Beisheng Group return the cooperative development fees of RMB 25 million obtained under the void contract, and compensate for interest losses of RMB 28,395,234.25 (calculated from the date Beisheng Group received the payments until the actual date of return, tentatively as of April 29, 2005).

Beisheng Group argued in defense: 1. Beihai Company did not establish a liquidation group in accordance with legal procedures to liquidate Weihao Company, and the company is not a party to the disputed contract; therefore, Beihai Company does not have standing as a plaintiff. 2. The nature of the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed by Weihao Company and Beisheng Group is the transfer of contractual rights and obligations. Beisheng Group originally agreed with the Investment Promotion Center that the Investment Promotion Center would provide the land and Beisheng Group would provide funds for joint cooperative land development. The contract signed between Beisheng Group and Weihao Company transferred Beisheng Group's funding obligation to Weihao Company. The contract did not violate mandatory legal provisions and is valid. Because Weihao Company failed to pay the full amount as agreed, Beisheng Group could not assist Weihao Company in obtaining the land use right, and Weihao Company itself should be responsible for this. 3. The lawsuit filed by Weihao Company exceeded the statutory limitation period. The "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" provided that Beisheng Group should handle the blue line map and contract conversion no later than 13 days from the date of signature of the contract. Beisheng Group did not complete these procedures within that period, and Weihao Company knew or should have known that its rights were infringed on March 16, 1993. Furthermore, in the other case, on January 26, 2000, the Intermediate People's Court of Beihai City, in its Civil Judgment (1999) Bei Min Chu Zi No. 66, determined that Weihao Company was unable to obtain the land use right and could not assist Hengtong Company in obtaining the land use right, and ordered Weihao Company to return the land payment and compensate for interest losses to Hengtong Company. When the Intermediate People's Court of Beihai City rendered that judgment, Weihao Company knew or should have known that its rights were infringed. The limitation period should at least start from that time. However, Weihao Company had never asserted its rights against Beisheng Group and did not file the lawsuit until 2005, which exceeded the statutory limitation period. Therefore, Beisheng Group requested the court to dismiss Weihao Company's claims.

The court of first instance considered after trial: The issues in dispute are: 1. Whether Beihai Company is a proper plaintiff in this case; 2. Whether the "Land Development Agreement" is void; 3. Whether the lawsuit filed by Weihao Company and Beihai Company exceeded the statutory limitation period.

Regarding the first issue, whether Beihai Company is a proper plaintiff: The court of first instance held that Beihai Company is a proper plaintiff in this case. Because Weihao Company is a wholly people-owned enterprise established by Beihai Company, after Weihao Company's business license was lawfully revoked by the administrative authority for industry and commerce, its capacity for civil conduct became limited to a certain extent, and no liquidation group has been established for liquidation to date. As the founding unit, supervisory authority, and sole investor of Weihao Company, Beihai Company has the right and obligation to clear up Weihao Company's claims and debts. It is not improper for this company to participate in the lawsuit as a co-plaintiff. Beisheng Group's argument that Beihai Company is not the contracting party of the contract with Weihao Company and therefore has no right to participate in the litigation is unfounded and is not supported.

Regarding the second issue, whether the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" is void: The court of first instance held that the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed by Weihao Company and Beisheng Group, though named as cooperative development, is in substance a transfer of land use right, and the agreement is a void contract. According to Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers to Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Real Estate Development and Operation Prior to the Implementation of the Law on the Administration of Real Estate," which provides: "A contract signed by a land user who has not obtained a land use certificate as the transferor with another party shall generally be deemed void; however, if the transferor has already invested and developed the land in accordance with the term and conditions stipulated in the assignment contract, and during the first instance proceedings, with the approval of the relevant competent authority, has gone through the formalities for registration or alteration registration of the land use right, the contract may be deemed valid." Beisheng Group, without obtaining the land use right for the disputed land, signed an agreement with Weihao Company to transfer the land use right, and neither actually invested in or developed the land, nor went through the relevant formalities for registration or alteration registration of the land use right during the first instance proceedings. Therefore, the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed by the parties is void. In accordance with the principle of restitution for void contracts, Beisheng Group shall return the land purchase price of RMB 25 million and interest thereon.

Beisheng Group argued in defense that the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" is valid, and the nature of the agreement is the transfer of contractual rights and obligations, i.e., Beisheng Group transferred its rights and obligations under the land cooperative development agreement with the Investment Promotion Center to Weihao Company. However, during the first instance proceedings, Beisheng Group could not provide the agreement signed with the Investment Promotion Center or other evidence to prove that it had a land cooperative development relationship with the Investment Promotion Center. Moreover, the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed between Beisheng Group and Weihao Company did not contain any clauses regarding joint investment, joint operation, or shared risks. On the contrary, Article 6 of the agreement stipulated that after Weihao Company paid the full amount, Beisheng Group would transfer the land use right to Weihao Company and handle the land use certificate for it. Clearly, the legal relationship between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group is not the transfer of rights and obligations under a land cooperative development contract, but rather a transfer of land use right. Even if the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" were a transfer of contractual rights and obligations, Beisheng Group's transfer would not have obtained the consent of the other party to the original contract, and such transfer would also be void. Therefore, Beisheng Group's defense that the contract is valid lacks factual and legal basis and is not accepted.

Beisheng Group also argued that Weihao Company failed to pay the full amount as agreed in the "Supplementary Agreement," which caused Beisheng Group to be unable to assist Weihao Company in obtaining the land use right, and Weihao Company should be responsible for this. The court of first instance held: In accordance with Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers to Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Real Estate Development and Operation Prior to the Implementation of the Law on the Administration of Real Estate," as the transferor of the land use right, Beisheng Group should have obtained the land use right before transferring it. Beisheng Group's transfer in this case violated the above provision. The fact that the transferee did not pay the full amount cannot legalize Beisheng Group's illegal conduct, nor is it the cause of the invalidity of the contract in question. Beisheng Group's defense is contrary to the provisions of the judicial interpretation and is not supported.

Regarding the third issue, whether the lawsuit filed by Weihao Company and Beihai Company exceeded the statutory limitation period: The court of first instance held that the lawsuit filed by Weihao Company and Beihai Company did not exceed the statutory limitation period. The limitation period for a party to request the court to protect civil rights is two years, and the limitation period starts from the date when the party knows or should know that its rights have been infringed. First, the two-year limitation period provided for in the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC applies to claims for creditor's rights, not to formative rights. Weihao Company and Beihai Company's request for confirmation that the contract is void falls under a formative rights action and should not be subject to the two-year limitation period. Second, the right to claim restitution of property arising from a void contract is in nature a claim for creditor's rights and should be subject to the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC on limitation periods. The limitation period starts from the date when the plaintiff knows or should know that its rights have been infringed. Given that parties do not have the legal power to confirm the invalidity of a contract, the right to claim restitution of unjust enrichment and the limitation period for that claim arise only after the contract is confirmed void by a statutory adjudicatory body. Therefore, only after the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group is declared void by the court does Weihao Company acquire the right to claim restitution of property. If Beisheng Group refuses to return the property, Weihao Company then knows or should know that its right has been infringed, and the limitation period begins to run. Taking the declaration of the contract void as the starting point of the limitation period for void contracts, the lawsuit filed by Weihao Company and Beihai Company did not exceed the statutory limitation period. Beisheng Group argues that taking the declaration of the contract void as the starting point of the limitation period may cause long-term instability in civil relations based on void contracts. However, the principle of limitation period reflects the state's public power's reasonable intervention in private rights, and the legislative preference and protection of public interest when it conflicts with private interest. At the same time, in litigation involving restitution of property based on void contracts, there is another interpretation in judicial practice regarding how to apply Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC: that the performance period of the void contract should be taken as the basis for determining the limitation period. The rationale is that parties to a void contract usually do not know that the contract is void before it is confirmed void by a statutory body, and they have a reasonable expectation of the contractual benefits set out in the void contract. If the void contract provides a performance period, after that period expires; if the contract does not provide a performance period, after the party asserts its rights and the other party still cannot fully perform its obligations, the party then knows or should know that its "contractual rights" have been infringed, and should actively exercise its litigation rights to protect its own interests. However, in this case, the parties did not agree on the time for performance of the land use right transfer, Weihao Company and Beihai Company never asserted their rights against Beisheng Group, and Beisheng Group never informed Weihao Company that it could not handle the land use right transfer procedures. Weihao Company did not know and should not have known that Beisheng Group could not perform. Therefore, whether the starting point of the limitation period is based on the declaration of the contract void by a statutory adjudicatory body or on the performance period of the void contract, the lawsuit filed by Weihao Company and Beihai Company in 2005 for restitution of property did not exceed the statutory limitation period.

Beisheng Group argued that the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" stipulated that Beisheng Group should complete the blue-line map and contract conversion for Weihao Company within thirteen days from the date of signing the contract. Beisheng Group failed to perform the above obligations within that time limit. Therefore, Weihao Company should have known that its rights were infringed, and the statute of limitations should begin to run. The court of first instance held that: First, the calculation of the statute of limitations for a contract should be based on the performance period of the principal obligations of the contract. Under the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement", the consideration for Weihao Company's payment of the land purchase price was Beisheng Group's transfer of the land use right to Weihao Company. Matters such as handling the blue-line map were merely collateral obligations. Their performance period cannot replace the performance period of the principal obligations of the contract, nor should it serve as the basis for determining the statute of limitations for the entire contract. Second, the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" stipulated that if Beisheng Group failed to handle the blue-line map and contract conversion within thirteen days from the date of signing the contract, the contract would remain valid and continue to be performed. In fact, after that time, both parties continued to perform the contract. It can be seen that the failure to timely handle the blue-line map and contract conversion did not affect the performance of other rights and obligations under the contract. Third, from a practical perspective, it is usually impossible to complete all procedures for the transfer of land use rights within thirteen days. Therefore, whether analyzed from the perspective of legal principles, contract terms, actual performance, or practical operation, although Beisheng Group failed to handle the blue-line map and other matters as agreed within thirteen days after the contract was signed, it cannot be inferred that Weihao Company knew or should have known that Beisheng Group could not perform its obligation to transfer the land use right.

In addition, Beisheng Group also argued that after the Beihai Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region rendered the Civil Judgment (1999) Bei Min Chu Zi No. 66, Weihao Company knew or should have known that its rights were infringed by Beisheng Group, and the statute of limitations period began to run. The court of first instance held that: The Beihai Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region tried the dispute between Weihao Company and Hengtong Company, and did not hear the dispute between the plaintiff and the defendant in this case. The judgment of the Beihai Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, which determined that the contract between Weihao Company and Hengtong Company could not be performed and was void, could not lead to the conclusion that the contract between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group was unperformable or void. There is no necessary logical relationship between the two. According to Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Real Estate Development and Operations Prior to the Implementation of the Real Estate Administration Law", the land use right transfer agreement between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group was, in substance, still in a state of pending validity at the time Weihao Company filed the lawsuit. That is, if Beisheng Group could complete the relevant land use right procedures during the first instance of this case, the contract could still be validly performed. Furthermore, the contract between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group did not stipulate a performance period for the transfer of the land use right. Although Weihao Company had litigation with Hengtong Company, Weihao Company still did not assert its rights against Beisheng Group, and Beisheng Group did not inform Weihao Company that it could not handle the land use right transfer procedures. Therefore, although Weihao Company lost the lawsuit against Hengtong Company, it cannot be presumed that Weihao Company knew or should have known that Beisheng Group had infringed its rights, thereby causing it to be unable to perform its contractual obligations with Hengtong Company.

In summary, as the sponsoring unit, competent authority, and sole investor of Weihao Company, Beihai Company has the right to participate in the litigation to liquidate Weihao Company's creditor's rights and debts. The "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group, though named as a cooperative development agreement, was in substance a transfer of land use rights. This agreement violated mandatory provisions of laws and regulations and is a void contract. Beisheng Group obtained RMB 25 million and interest as payment for land without legal basis and should return it. The lawsuit filed by Weihao Company and Beihai Company complies with the legal provisions on the statute of limitations, and their right of action should be protected by law. Pursuant to Article 61, Paragraph 1, Article 92, Article 135, Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Real Estate Development and Operations Prior to the Implementation of the Real Estate Administration Law", and after discussion and decision by the Adjudication Committee of the court of first instance, the judgment is as follows: (1) The "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group on March 3, 1993, is a void contract; (2) Beisheng Group shall return RMB 25 million and interest to Weihao Company and Beihai Company (interest shall be calculated from the date Beisheng Group received the payment until the expiration of the performance period specified in the judgment, based on the one-year time deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period). The obligor shall perform the above obligations within fifteen days from the date the judgment takes effect; otherwise, the debt interest during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled. The case acceptance fee of RMB 282,986 shall be borne by Beisheng Group.

Beisheng Group, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, requesting: 1. To set aside the judgment of first instance; 2. To dismiss all claims of Weihao Company and Beihai Company; 3. To order Weihao Company and Beihai Company to bear all litigation costs of this case.

(1) Beihai Company is not a proper plaintiff in this case. Although as the sponsoring unit, competent authority, and sole investor of Weihao Company, Beihai Company has the right and obligation to liquidate Weihao Company's creditor's rights and debts, there is no legal provision that before a legal person is dissolved, its sponsoring unit has the right to participate in litigation as a party on its behalf or jointly. This fundamentally violates the principle of legal person independence. The civil rights capacity and civil conduct capacity of a legal person arise upon its establishment and terminate upon its dissolution. Although Weihao Company was established upon application by Beihai Company, after its business license was revoked according to law, it did not undergo liquidation under an organization including its sponsoring unit Beihai Company, nor did it complete the cancellation of registration. Therefore, Weihao Company remains an independent legal person existing according to law. The revocation of the business license does not affect Weihao Company's right to maintain independent civil rights capacity and other civil conduct capacities according to law. Weihao Company still has the right and can only independently exercise the various civil rights conferred by law in its own name, including participating in litigation. Therefore, the court of first instance's determination that Beihai Company is a proper plaintiff in this case is clearly erroneous.

(2) Weihao Company's lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations. 1. The court of first instance's determination that "the plaintiff's claim for confirming the voidness of the contract is a right of formation action and should not be subject to the two-year statute of limitations" has no legal basis. Our country's laws do not clearly stipulate whether a claim for confirming a void contract is subject to the statute of limitations, and there has always been some controversy in both theory and practice. Our country is a statutory law country. In the absence of a clear legal provision that void contracts are not subject to the statute of limitations, the people's court should not and should not use controversial academic theories or doctrines as the basis for deciding the case. It should equally apply the legal provisions on the statute of limitations, i.e., a limit of two years. 2. The court of first instance's determination that "the statute of limitations for a void contract begins from the time the contract is declared void" is erroneous. The court of first instance held that "since the parties do not enjoy the statutory power to confirm the voidness of a contract, only after the contract is confirmed as void by a statutory adjudicatory authority does the claim for restitution of property based on unjust enrichment arise, and along with it, the issue of the statute of limitations for that claim." Beisheng Group believes that whether a contract is valid does not affect the party's right to assert its claims. Therefore, confirming the voidness of a contract and the claim for restitution of property are two issues that can and should be separated. The court cannot disregard legal provisions and presume on its own when Weihao Company knew its rights were impaired; otherwise, the statute of limitations would become a dead letter. Moreover, although the voidness of a contract involves illegal factors, the property involved in this case is within the scope of the parties' free disposition, pertains to private rights, and is not a matter that the state must proactively intervene in. Simply taking the date the contract is declared void as the starting point of the statute of limitations for the claim for restitution of property would inevitably keep civil relationships based on void contracts in a long-term unstable state, which is detrimental to the healthy development of the entire socio-economic life. 3. Whether a right holder's rights are infringed is a matter of value judgment to be determined by a statutory adjudicatory authority. However, whether the right holder knows or should know that its rights are infringed is a factual issue to be established by evidence. The judgment that the land transfer contract between Weihao Company and Hengtong Company was void indeed cannot lead to the conclusion that the contract in this case is void, thereby establishing that Weihao Company's rights were infringed. However, it can be used to determine that Weihao Company should have known that its own rights were infringed. First, Beisheng Group had no use right over the disputed land and had not actually invested in or developed the land. After more than ten years, it still could not complete the land transfer procedures. The land transfer contract with Weihao Company violated mandatory legal provisions and was highly likely to be declared void. Second, Weihao Company had already assumed legal liability towards Hengtong Company and suffered significant economic losses. The fact that Weihao Company's rights were infringed had already occurred. Weihao Company, however, was negligent in exercising its rights and never asserted claims against Beisheng Group, causing the statute of limitations period to expire.

Weihao Company and Beihai Company argued in their defense that the judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact and correct application of law and should be affirmed. Beisheng Group's grounds of appeal cannot be established and should be dismissed.

(1) Regarding the issue of Beihai Company's standing. Beihai Company is the sponsoring unit of Weihao Company. On November 26, 2003, the Beihai Administration for Industry and Commerce of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region revoked Weihao Company's business license and ordered liquidation by the sponsoring unit, investors, or liquidation group. To date, Weihao Company has not established a liquidation group. Therefore, as the sponsoring unit, Beihai Company has the right and obligation to carry out the liquidation of Weihao Company's creditor's rights and debts. This lawsuit is part of the liquidation work for Weihao Company's creditor's rights and debts. Beihai Company's joint participation in the lawsuit together with Weihao Company, whose rights and obligations are already restricted, complies with legal provisions.

(2) Regarding the issue of the statute of limitations. Weihao Company's lawsuit has not exceeded the statute of limitations, and its claims should be supported by the court. 1. The confirmation of voidness of a void contract is not subject to the statute of limitations. The statute of limitations period for the claim for restitution of property arising from a void contract should begin from the date the contract is confirmed void. The confirmation of voidness of a contract is not subject to the statute of limitations. The voidness of a contract is the result of the intervention of public power represented by law in the process of contract formation. Confirming the validity of a contract falls within the realm of value judgment. As long as laws or administrative regulations deem the contract void or harmful to public interests, the contract should be declared void without regard to the time that has passed since the contract was made. Moreover, the statute of limitations system applies to claims for creditor's rights, while confirming the voidness of a contract is a right of formation, and an action to confirm voidness is a declaratory action, not subject to the statute of limitations. The voidness of a contract is a legal status. The law should not compel parties to constantly scrutinize the validity of their contracts, thereby rendering transactions in an uncertain state. While a party is performing a contract in good faith, the issue of the statute of limitations for asserting claims regarding the validity of the contract and the disposition of property under a void contract does not arise. The statute of limitations period for a claim for restitution of property arising from a void contract should begin from the date the contract is confirmed void. If, under the pretext of "stability of civil relations," a void contract could, through the passage of time, achieve the same factual result as a valid contract, that would clearly violate the legislative purpose. 2. Even if the statute of limitations for a void contract should begin from the date the party knew or should have known that its rights were infringed, Beisheng Group's argument that Weihao Company's claims are time-barred cannot be sustained. First, the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group did not stipulate a performance period for the principal obligation. For a contract without a performance period, according to relevant provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law and the Contract Law of our country, the statute of limitations begins to run as follows: (1) If upon the creditor's demand the debtor immediately indicates performance but fails to perform, the statute of limitations begins from the day after the demand; (2) If the parties agree on a definite performance period through consultation, the statute of limitations begins from the day after the expiration of that period; if the parties cannot agree on a performance period, after either party proposes a reasonable performance period, the statute of limitations begins from the day after that reasonable period; (3) If the creditor asserts its claim against the debtor, and the debtor immediately and expressly refuses, and such refusal implies an intention not to perform the debt in the future, then the statute of limitations begins from the day after the date of such refusal. In this case, none of the above situations exist. Therefore, there is no fact that Weihao Company knew or should have known that its rights were infringed, and the statute of limitations has not begun to run. In reality, it was the parties themselves who, taking into account the condition of the real estate industry in Beihai City and from the perspective of maximizing the interests of both parties, mutually recognized that the contract was in a continuous factual state. Therefore, there is no circumstance of rights being infringed. 3. The validity of the contract between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group cannot be determined by the parties or any third party without a ruling by an adjudicatory authority. Weihao Company cannot rely on a judgment in another case to subjectively infer that its rights under this contract were infringed. In fact, when Weihao Company entered into the cooperative development contract with the third party, it was unclear when Beisheng Group would actually obtain the land use right for the disputed plot. Weihao Company had a reasonable expectation of a possible default towards the third party arising from this and was willing to assume that risk. Even if Beisheng Group could not obtain the state-owned land use right for the plot within the time limit agreed between Weihao Company and the third party, Weihao Company could not unilaterally presume Beisheng Group's default. Moreover, after the dispute between Weihao Company and Hengtong Company was adjudicated by the Beihai Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region in its Civil Judgment (1999) Bei Min Chu Zi No. 66, up until before the first instance of this case, it was still possible for Beisheng Group to legally obtain the state-owned land use right for the agreed plot and then transfer it to Weihao Company as stipulated in the contract. In fact, the contract between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group was not absolutely void. If Beisheng Group could obtain the state-owned land use right for the disputed land during the first instance of this case, the contract could still be deemed valid. The fact that Weihao Company failed to obtain the state-owned land use right for the disputed plot during the first instance of another lawsuit does not mean that Beisheng Group could not obtain it later. According to the spirit of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Real Estate Development and Operations Prior to the Implementation of the Real Estate Administration Law", if Beisheng Group could obtain the state-owned land use right for the disputed land during the first instance of this case, the cooperative development contract between the parties could still be deemed valid. In fact, at that time, Weihao Company's rights were not yet infringed. Until just before filing the lawsuit, Weihao Company and Beihai Company still hoped that Beisheng Group would continue to perform its obligation to deliver the land use right. However, Beisheng Group has been unable to complete this contractual obligation to date, directly leading to the voidness of the cooperative development contract.

The facts found by this Court in the second instance are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

This Court holds that there are two main points of contention between the parties in the second instance of this case: First, whether Beihai Company has standing as a plaintiff; Second, whether Weihao Company's lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations.

(1) Whether Beihai Company has standing as a plaintiff.

Upon investigation, Weihao Company was established upon application by Beihai Company. Because Weihao Company failed to submit its annual industrial and commercial inspection as required, on November 26, 2003, the Beihai Administration for Industry and Commerce of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region issued an administrative penalty decision deciding to revoke Weihao Company's business license. However, to date, no liquidation group has been established to carry out liquidation. According to Article 36 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China: "A legal person is an organization that has the capacity for civil rights and the capacity for civil conduct, and independently enjoys civil rights and assumes civil obligations in accordance with the law. The capacity for civil rights and the capacity for civil conduct of a legal person arise upon its establishment and terminate upon its dissolution." Article 38 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Company Registration stipulates: "Upon approval of the cancellation of registration by the company registration authority, the company terminates." Although Weihao Company was established upon application by Beihai Company, after its business license was lawfully revoked, it did not undergo liquidation nor did it complete the cancellation of registration. Therefore, Weihao Company still enjoys the capacity for civil litigation rights and the capacity for civil conduct, i.e., it has the right to participate in civil litigation in its own name. Although Beihai Company, as the sponsoring unit of Weihao Company, has the right and obligation to liquidate Weihao Company's creditor's rights and debts, there is no legal basis for the sponsoring unit to participate in litigation jointly as a party when Weihao Company has not yet been dissolved. Beihai Company is not a party to the contract signed between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group and has no direct civil legal relationship with Beisheng Group. Therefore, the court of first instance's determination that Beihai Company is a proper plaintiff in this case lacks legal basis. Beisheng Group's appeal ground that Beihai Company does not have standing as a plaintiff in this case should be upheld.

(2) Whether Weihao Company's lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations.

The court of first instance held that the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group, though named as a cooperative development agreement, was in substance a transfer of land use rights. Because Beisheng Group, without having obtained the use right to the disputed land, signed the agreement to transfer the use right of that land to Weihao Company, and neither actually invested in or developed the land nor completed the relevant land use right registration or alteration procedures during the first instance of this case, the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed between the parties should be void. The court of first instance's above findings regarding the nature and validity of the contract are consistent with the facts of this case, and the application of law is correct. Moreover, both parties have no objection to the validity of the contract.

Pursuant to Article 135 and Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the statute of limitations for a party to request the People's Court to protect its civil rights is two years, and the statute of limitations period shall begin from the time when the party knew or should have known that its rights were infringed. This Court holds that the parties to a contract do not enjoy the statutory right to confirm the voidness of a contract; only arbitral institutions and people's courts have the authority to confirm whether a contract is valid. The determination of a contract's validity essentially involves the intervention of state public power in civil conduct. A void contract is void ab initio; the mere passage of time cannot change the illegality of a void contract. A party's request to confirm the voidness of a contract should not be subject to the statute of limitations. However, after a contract is confirmed void, a party's claim for restitution of property and damages should be subject to the legal provisions on the statute of limitations. In this case, only after the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group was confirmed void by the People's Court did Weihao Company have a claim for restitution of property. Therefore, Weihao Company's lawsuit has not exceeded the statutory statute of limitations period.

Beisheng Group argued that the "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed by both parties stipulated that Beisheng Group should, within 13 days from the date of signing the contract, handle the blue-line map and conversion contract for Weihao Company. Since Beisheng Group failed to perform the above obligations within that period, Weihao Company should have known that its rights were infringed, and the statute of limitations should begin to run. This Court holds that: The "Land Cooperative Development Agreement" signed by both parties stipulated that if Beisheng Group failed to handle the blue-line map and conversion contract within 13 days from the date of signing the contract, the contract would remain valid and enforceable, except that Beisheng Group should bear corresponding liability for breach of contract, i.e., compensate Weihao Company RMB 1 million. Therefore, the contract remained in a state of ongoing performance; the failure to timely handle the blue-line map and conversion contract did not affect the performance of other rights and obligations under the contract, and moreover, the above obligation was not a principal obligation under the contract between the parties. Hence, although Beisheng Group did not handle the blue-line map and other matters within 13 days after the contract was signed as agreed, it cannot be inferred therefrom that Weihao Company knew or should have known that Beisheng Group was unable to perform the obligation to transfer the land use right. The ground of appeal raised by Beisheng Group on this point cannot be sustained.

Beisheng Group also argued on appeal that after the Beihai Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region rendered the civil judgment (1999) Bei Min Chu Zi No. 66, Weihao Company knew or should have known that its rights were infringed by Beisheng Group, and the limitation period should begin to run. This Court holds that: The court of first instance had sufficient reasoning and basis for its determination on this issue. The Beihai Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region tried the dispute between Weihao Company and Hengtong Company, which has no direct connection with this case. The judgment of the Beihai Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region that found the contract between Weihao Company and Hengtong Company invalid cannot lead to the inference that the contract between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group is also invalid. Pursuant to Article 7 of the "Answers to Several Questions Concerning the Trial of Real Estate Development and Operation Cases Before the Implementation of the Real Estate Administration Law" of the Supreme People's Court, the land use right transfer agreement between Weihao Company and Beisheng Group was in a state of pending validity at the time Weihao Company filed the lawsuit, i.e., if Beisheng Group could supplement the relevant procedures for the land use right during the first-instance trial of this case, the contract could still be valid and performable. Moreover, Beisheng Group did not inform Weihao Company that it could not complete the procedures for the transfer of the land use right. Therefore, although Weihao Company lost the lawsuit against Hengtong Company, it cannot be presumed therefrom that Weihao Company knew or should have known that Beisheng Group had infringed its rights. The ground of appeal raised by Beisheng Group on this point also cannot be sustained.

In summary, in accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm item 1 of the civil judgment (2005) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 3 of the Guangxi High People's Court;

2. Amend item 2 of the civil judgment (2005) Gui Min Yi Chu Zi No. 3 of the Guangxi High People's Court to: Guangxi Beisheng Group Co., Ltd. shall, within 15 days from the date this judgment becomes effective, return RMB 25 million to Beihai Weihao Real Estate Development Company, plus interest (interest shall be calculated from the date of receipt of the funds at the one-year deposit rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period).

Total court fees for first instance and second instance: RMB 565,972, to be borne by Guangxi Beisheng Group Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
